theme_note: These codes all recruit or hand work to people so a Pitt mark can begin or continue. What varies is whether someone asks for a design, volunteers personally, joins an expansion, or leaves the next shift to people still awake.

second_order: laying out the logo pixel by pixel
theme_note: These codes turn an intended mark into a workable pixel plan. They vary across choosing a spot, colours, outlines, coordinates, spacing, size, and later designs such as Cathy.

second_order: building, cleaning, and holding the Pitt work
theme_note: These codes do the recurring hands-on work of placing, cleaning, maintaining, and defending pixels. What varies is whether participants are filling, repairing, expanding, watching the main logo, or treating damage as easy cleanup.

second_order: choosing the Pitt work over bigger fights
theme_note: These codes narrow the task when resistance, people, space, or maintenance make larger ambitions costly. They vary from refocusing on Pitt, keeping a design small, stopping attacks, declining more expansion, and giving up a lost H2P.

These codes work out who can occupy adjacent or overlapping space. They vary from alliance and compromise proposals to intrusion, repair, mutual-respect agreements, direct border promises, and relaying a correction through Discord.

second_order: keeping r/place talk in one megathread
theme_note: These codes are moderator-led attempts to collect scattered r/place posts and suggestions in one thread. They vary from declaring the megathread and removing an attack post to repeated redirects and participants apologising or complying.

second_order: putting the canvas logo back on r/Pitt
theme_note: These codes carry the canvas-made logo into the subreddit's own display. They vary across proposing the reuse, implementing it, noticing a damaged screenshot, and correcting it.

These codes publicly value the shared work. They vary from counting a second of visibility as worthwhile to pride in helpers, congratulations, jokes about Pitt doing Reddit, and admiration of neighboring finished work.

second_order: telling how the canvas work was going
theme_note: These codes keep others oriented by reporting progress, setbacks, changed appearances, and the ending. They vary from a completed digit or nearly finished P to saying the presence improved and recounting what remained at closure.

second_order: calling out attacks and getting back on defense
theme_note: These codes alert others to threats or name their apparent source so defense can follow. They vary from Penn State and Ohio State sightings to neighboring claims, script warnings, invasions, and direct calls to defend.
